summary: This Odyssey lecture presses a reusable moral-repair mechanism: war and victory can shatter the soul/worldview when noble reasons invert into murder, family destruction, and shame, and homecoming requires poetic memory, family love, and self-recognition rather than mere return to place.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Odysseus can go home only after the Trojan horse memory forces him to see Penelope in the Trojan widow and confront himself as a destroyer of families.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Human Heart already owns forgiveness, guilt, memory, and the inward battlefield. This source is not yet linked in episode JSON, but these marks are strong candidates for a later concept-scoped provenance batch if the Heart/Odyssey repair layer becomes public.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: A banquet song becomes the therapeutic trap: heroic public memory makes Odysseus cry because memory is storing pain in him.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Poetry owns living memory and performed song as the medium through which a character's world becomes active again. The active mechanism is not generic Odyssey content; it is poetry forcing repressed moral memory into view.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Odysseus' fake madness is a clever failure that lets him be forced into the war he half wants, so his later brokenness remains tied to his own divided desire and responsibility.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Free Will owns the responsibility layer: Odysseus is not only victimized by war; his desire for glory and self-excusing strategy participate in the wound he later must repair.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The Trojan horse appears here before the Roman inversion as Odysseus' own traumatic memory: glorious offering and concealed engine of death at once.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This should not be appended to Imperial Poetry as ordinary Roman material. It is Homeric source pressure for the original wound that later Roman poetry will recode.

new_lens_seeds.title: Home After Evil
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: A person cannot return home merely by reaching the place when the story that made home meaningful has been shattered by moral injury; repair requires facing the memory of harm, recognizing the victim as kin, and rebuilding the soul/worldview so family and action become possible again.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism travels beyond the Odyssey: it can compare war trauma, self-forgiveness, enemy-recognition, poetic memory, family repair, and Jiang's later Dante material on self-made hell and self-redemption without becoming a generic PTSD or Odyssey topic.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed, not a standalone Odyssey, Odysseus, PTSD, Moral Injury, or Homecoming page. Promote only after comparing with existing Human Heart forgiveness, Free Will self-redemption, and Poetry living-memory anchors.

new_lens_seeds.title: Soul As Worldview Rupture
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: The ancient soul becomes Jiang's richer version of worldview: a layered relational field of family, culture, history, and gods; trauma breaks it when a central fact is too painful to integrate, producing depression as inability to act, think, want, or judge.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The source gives a compact diagnostic model for many Jiang pages that discuss attention, education, cave reality, heart, and free will, but it should remain a seed until more sources show the same soul/worldview translation as an explicit repeated mechanism.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed. Do not create a standalone Soul, Worldview, Depression, PTSD, or Trauma page from this source alone; route by active mechanism until a cluster proves a public concept is needed.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2026-03-04, this lecture sits after the January Homer/Achilles source and before the April Dante self-made-hell source. It supplies the Odysseus layer of moral injury and homecoming: guilt and divided desire must become conscious before love and family can repair the soul.

This source makes bardic performance a memory-repair device before the later Paradiso and Dante/Virgil method layers: poetry does not only preserve heroic deeds; it can force the listener to confront the hidden moral cost of those deeds.

The Trojan horse appears here as Odysseus' own traumatic Homeric memory before the Aeneid turns Greek culture and Homeric values into a Roman training problem. Keep the source as comparison pressure unless a later public edit explicitly contrasts original wound with Roman inversion.
